title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter III of the 1986 notes on 'réseaux via découpages' belongs to Grothendieck's programme of tame ('modérée') topology. The previous page (9 June) starts studying an ordered 'tronçon' L. It is apparently partially ordered: the comparison 'b ⊃ a' suggests its elements are subsets ordered by inclusion inside an ambient H. L carries a 'canonical' topology with open base the intervals ]a,b[ (a<b), together with the rays L_{<a} and L_{>b}. Page 21 notes that a point need not be closed, and that b lies in the closure of {a} iff b ⊃ a. So the specialization preorder of the topology is the given order (or its opposite).

This page draws the consequences.
(1) Since the specialization preorder is the order, cl{a} = cl{b} iff a = b, so L is T0.
(2) A T0 space is exactly one whose canonical map to its sobrification is injective; Grothendieck calls such spaces 'pristin'. He asks, without answering, whether a lattice ('treillis') with its canonical topology is always sober. Sobriety would mean every irreducible closed set has a unique generic point.
(3) Consequently, in the non-total case the order segments [a,b] are not closed in the canonical topology.
(4) Only for a totally ordered L can one expect points to be closed (he wonders about the converse). In that case L is Hausdorff, which is correct for the order topology on a chain. The sets [a,b], L_{≥a} and L_{≤a} are then closed.
(5) He proposes a second topology whose closed sets are generated by [a,b], L_{≥a}, L_{≤a}: arbitrary intersections of finite unions. This is exactly Frink's interval topology on a poset or lattice; the [a,b] are redundant, being L_{≥a} ∩ L_{≤b}.

The next page observes that in this topology ]a,b[ is no longer open. He then takes the topology generated by both families and tests whether cl(]a,b[) = [a,b], finding a counterexample.

Purpose: to find a good topology on ordered sets of 'découpages' or strata, compatible with the tame-topology formalism.
errors: No real errors. Two minor points: (i) [a,b] is redundant in the proposed closed subbase, since [a,b] = L_{≥a} ∩ L_{≤b}. (ii) For a totally ordered L the new topology coincides with the canonical (order) topology, since the complements of the subbasic closed sets are the rays L_{<a}, L_{>a}. So the second topology only differs, and only matters, in the non-total case, which the page does not make explicit.
The sobriety question for lattices is left open. For comparable topologies it is known to fail in general (e.g. Johnstone's 1981 non-sober Scott topology on a complete lattice).

ideas.what: The specialization order of the canonical (open-interval) topology on a poset recovers the order, hence the space is T0
T0 iff the space injects into its sobrification (term 'pristin')
ideas.where_published: EGA I (0, §2.1) and SGA 4 Exp. IV for sober spaces; the word 'pristin' seems unpublished

ideas.what: Question whether a lattice with its canonical order topology is sober
ideas.modern_name: sobriety of order topologies (Scott, Alexandrov, interval topologies) on lattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Johnstone (1981), Isbell; Gierz et al. 'Continuous Lattices and Domains'

ideas.what: Topology with closed subbase the principal up-sets and down-sets L_{≥a}, L_{≤a}
Order topology of a totally ordered set is Hausdorff, with closed intervals and rays

deep.surprise_reason: Routine exploration of order topologies on posets and lattices; Grothendieck essentially rediscovers Frink's interval topology and the known sobriety question. The only minor curiosity is his private term 'pristin' for T0 (injecting into the sobrification) and the tame-topology context.
transcription_corrections: 'tot ordonné' is 'tout ordonné' / 'totalement ordonné' (the word 'tot' is underlined in the image).
'prisobifié[?]' is probably 'sobrifié' (the sobrification), since 'pristin' is glossed as 'injects into the sobrified space'.
The last line likely reads '(c'est-à-dire on prend les intersections quelconques des réunions finies, pour avoir tous les fermés)', with 'fermés' on the final line.
